root_cause.text: `net/802/mrp.c::mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()` had incorrect `valen`/attribute-value state management in the MRP VectorAttribute parser, so it misparsed zero-length and multi-event vector fields by consuming absent FirstValue data and failing to advance/decrement correctly across encoded events.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early `if (valen == 0) return 0;` because “FirstValue and Vector fields are absent,” and in the event loop it adds `valen--;` plus `mrp_attrvalue_inc(...)` after processing the third event, matching the commit note that the old code “decrements valen after processing the first and second events… but not after processing the third one” and did not increment the attribute value between bytes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip vector-attribute parsing when valen is zero so LeaveAll-only MRP PDUs are handled correctly.
intent_record.what: In mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr(), after extracting valen from the Vector Attribute header, the function now checks whether valen is 0 and immediately returns 0 in that case, with a new comment explaining that this means only a LeaveAllEvent is present and that FirstValue and Vector fields are absent per IEEE 802.1ak.
intent_record.how: This prevents the parser from continuing to interpret a Vector Attribute payload when no vector/value data is present, avoiding incorrect parsing of LeaveAll-only PDUs and treating them as a valid no-op case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Advance the vector attribute parser state after each event so all values are consumed correctly.
intent_record.what: Inside `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()`, after calling `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr_event(app, skb, vaevent);`, the code now decrements `valen` and calls `mrp_attrvalue_inc(mrp_cb(skb)->attrvalue, mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen);` before the loop continues.
intent_record.how: This changes the per-iteration parsing state so the vector-attribute parser advances the attribute value pointer/offset by the current attribute length and tracks one fewer remaining value, preventing the same value from being processed repeatedly and allowing subsequent values to be parsed correctly.

Advance the vector attribute parser state after each event so all values are consumed correctly.

Author: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>

    net/802: Implement Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    
    Initial implementation of the Multiple Registration Protocol (MRP)
    from IEEE 802.1Q-2011, based on the existing implementation of the
    Generic Attribute Registration Protocol (GARP).
    
    Signed-off-by: David Ward <david.ward@ll.mit.edu>
    Acked-by: Patrick McHardy <kaber@trash.net>
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr()` does contain the VectorAttribute parsing logic, including `valen = be16_to_cpu(... & MRP_VECATTR_HDR_LEN_MASK);` and the loop that consumes events with `while (valen > 0) { ... if (!--valen) break; ... }`. However, the vulnerable root cause describes incorrect `valen`/attribute-value state management for zero-length and multi-event vector fields (consuming absent FirstValue data and failing to advance/decrement correctly). In this initial implementation, the parser explicitly rejects zero-length message attributes earlier in `mrp_pdu_parse_msg()` with `if (mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrtype == 0 || mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrtype > app->app->maxattr || mrp_cb(skb)->mh->attrlen == 0) return -1;`, so the zero-length case is not accepted here. The vector parsing also always copies the first attribute value before processing events, and the event count is handled by decrementing `valen` after each extracted event. Nothing in this snippet shows the later bug fix because this is the original implementation, but the specific vulnerable construct described is not clearly present as a reachable defect in this function body alone.
